## Developer Guide

If you are new to using `nbdev` here are some useful pointers to get you
started.

### Install richcal in Development mode

``` sh
# make sure richcal package is installed in development mode
$ pip install -e .

# make changes under nbs/ directory
# ...

# compile to have changes apply to richcal
$ nbdev_prepare
```

## Usage

### Installation

Install latest from the GitHub
[repository](https://github.com/doyu/richcal):

``` sh
$ pip install git+https://github.com/doyu/richcal.git
```

or from [conda](https://anaconda.org/doyu/richcal)

``` sh
$ conda install -c doyu richcal
```

or from [pypi](https://pypi.org/project/richcal/)

``` sh
$ pip install richcal
```

### Documentation

Documentation can be found hosted on this GitHub
[repository](https://github.com/doyu/richcal)’s
[pages](https://doyu.github.io/richcal/). Additionally you can find
package manager specific guidelines on
[conda](https://anaconda.org/doyu/richcal) and
[pypi](https://pypi.org/project/richcal/) respectively.

## How to use

``` python
from datetime import date, timedelta
from rich.console import Console
from richcal import CalendarHeatmap

data = {date(2026, 1, 1) + timedelta(days=i): (i * 7) % 23 for i in range(170)}
Console().print(CalendarHeatmap(data, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31), as_of=date(2026, 6, 23)))
```
